limit: fa_goodput_bps=26036198 is capped by fa's scheduler raw-bit share at lc.queue.parts.fa=0.185 after packet-header overhead; larger tested parts.fa violates fb_loss_frac because fb's 80 Mbps offer exceeds its scheduler payload share, and lc.queue.length=1000 only delays/buffers packets beyond the measured window rather than increasing service (E6, E7, C9, C10, V9, V10, C11, V11).
explanation: The scheduler divides raw lc bits by the parts and is work-conserving, so fa's payload goodput is its raw scheduler share reduced by header overhead. At the feasible boundary fa is backlogged, so changing fa.type or increasing lc.queue.length does not raise fa_goodput by more than tolerance; it only removes fa drops or delays fb packets. Increasing lc.queue.length from 100 to 1000 lowers measured fb_loss_frac by buffering about 900 extra packets and increasing maximum fb wait, moving the tested feasible parts.fa from 0.180 to 0.185 while leaving fa and fb goodputs unchanged. p0185_len1000 is the largest tested setting satisfying fb_loss_frac <= 0.1; p0188_len1000 gives higher fa_goodput but fb_loss_frac=0.104301.

claims.text: The scheduler divides raw lc bits and is work-conserving when a flow underuses its part.
fa_goodput at the boundary is set by scheduler share and header overhead, not by fa.type or queue capacity.
lc.queue.length=1000 lowers fb_loss_frac without changing delivered goodput by increasing queue delay and buffering beyond the measured window.
The tested feasible boundary with length=1000 is at parts.fa=0.185; parts.fa=0.188 violates fb_loss_frac.
TcpCubic is recommended because no tested congestion control raised fa_goodput by more than tolerance at the scheduler-limited boundary.
